newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-PSG PLAN TO HANG ON TO LEONARDO.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PSG PLAN TO HANG ON TO LEONARDO.

text.p: Paris St Germain plan to hang on to midfielder Leonardo who has been courted by leading European clubs since helping Brazil win the Copa America last month.
"The player wants to stay in Paris and the club aims to keep him," PSG executive president Michel Denisot told the sports daily L'Equipe.
"Practically all the best European clubs want him in their squad. But, unless there is an extraordinary offer which we would then study, Leonardo will be with us next season.
"Besides, he's still under contract with PSG for two seasons and the opt out clause in his contract is only valid for a return to Brazil."
Leonardo, who had an excellent Tournoi de France and Copa America in June, has been linked with Barcelona and AC Milan in the last few weeks.

Denisot was in Geneva for Wednesday's draw of the three European club competitions in which PSG were landed with a tough European Cup second preliminary round clash against either former winners Steaua Bucharest or CSKA Sofia next month.
"It's a difficult draw, the most difficult we could have had with the winners of Partizan Belgrade-Croatia Zagreb," he said.
PSG will be away to the Romanian or Bulgarian champions on August 13, after they have played just two league games, with the second leg at home on August 27.

"This match will be extremely important with a lot at stake both on the field and financially. As I've already said several times, it is vital for the club to qualify for the Champions' League," Denisot said.
PSG qualified for the preliminary rounds after finishing runners-up to Monaco in the French first division last season.
The club's new sporting director Claude Le Roy said: "They (Romania and Bulgaria) are two quality footballing countries but they too won't be happy to come up against PSG."
Manager Ricardo said PSG, who have strengthened their squad considerably in the close season, would have to accelerate their training programme to be better tuned for the European Cup matches.

Italian striker Marco Simone became the club's most expensive recruit ever when he signed from AC Milan for nearly $7 million at the end of June on an annual salary of more than $2.7 million for four years.

PSG have also spent $6.5 million on France striker Florian Maurice, who they signed from Lyon along with forward Franck Gava, while goalkeeper Christophe Revault was transferred from Le Havre for $3.2 million.
In the league, PSG kick off at home to promoted Chateauroux on August 2 and travel to 1996 champions Auxerre a week later.
They wind up their pre-season programme in a four-team tournament in Berlin with German champions Bayern Munich, AC Milan and Hertha Berlin in the last week of July.
